To evaluate the effects of whey protein peptide-ferrous chelate (WPP-Fe) on iron deficiency anemia (IDA), this study investigated its influence on iron metabolism, oxidative stress, and gut microbiota in IDA mice.
This suggests that whey protein peptide-ferrous (WPP-Fe) chelate, constructed using whey protein peptides as carriers, may outperform conventional organic iron supplements and function as a multifunctional system integrating efficient iron supplementation, intestinal protection, and gut microbiota regulation. Previous studies have demonstrated that WPP-Fe chelate exhibits significantly superior in vitro stability, iron absorption efficiency, and antioxidant activity compared with ferrous chloride (FeCl₂) and ferrous gluconate (Fe-gluc) (Wu, Wang, Ma, Mu, & Qian, 2024).
The results showed that medium-dose WPP-Fe (2.0 mg Fe/kg BW) exhibited superior efficacy compared with ferrous chloride (FeCl₂) and ferrous gluconate (Fe-gluc). WPP-Fe significantly increased hemoglobin levels (156.35 ± 3.75 g/L) and iron bioavailability (331.9 ± 43.88%), while alleviating oxidative stress through regulation of inflammatory cytokines and enhancement of antioxidant capacity.
